svg.title: Drempel and the Vonk: the pitchfork of one Koppel, and the Marge of a whole
svg.desc: Two bifurcation diagrams of the order parameter φ against the binding B (Section VIII.3 of the Speelgoed). Left, one Koppel seen alone, the symmetric limit V(φ; B) = ¼·φ⁴ − ½·(B − θ)·φ²: below the Drempel θ the only stable point is φ = 0, Van; above it φ = 0 becomes unstable and two Naar modes appear at ±√(B − θ). A small sketch of V(φ) shows the two equal wells above θ, each lying the Energie T = ¼·(B − θ)² below φ = 0. Right, a whole, in one shape it could take (the Speelgoed gives it no formula): its two Naar modes are not mirror images. Both are entered at the same edge of a band around θ, where Van gives way, and each is left at its own fold further back, one far, one close. The way into a mode is never the way out; that band is the Marge (η). Inside it Van and Naar stay open side by side, and a whole keeps the mode it came from until something wider than the Marge carries it across. Every crossing fires a Vonk: toward Naar a Realisatie, a Winst; toward Van a Schok, a Verlies.
svg.text: §VIII.3 · ONE KOPPEL SEEN ALONE, AND A WHOLE
the symmetric limit: V(φ; B) = ¼·φ⁴ − ½·(B − θ)·φ²
one shape it could take; the Speelgoed gives it no formula
Each mode is entered where Van gives way and
left at its own fold, one far back, one close. Inside
the Marge, Van and Naar stay open side by side;
a whole keeps the mode it came from until
something wider than the Marge carries it across.
No Koppel occurs alone. The Vonk (q) fires at every crossing:
toward Naar a Realisatie, a Winst (+); toward Van a Schok, a Verlies (−).
